issue.title: Replace the per-provider string allowlists in sase-core indicator.rs with declared window classification
issue.description:
Replace the accumulated per-provider string allowlists in the sase-core crate's `provider_usage/indicator.rs` with a data-driven classification the providers themselves declare.

Today `is_weekly_window` resolves a window's period from `duration_seconds` first and otherwise falls through to a hard-coded chain of `provider == "<name>"` string arms; epic sase-14c added the third such arm (`provider == "muse" && key == "weekly" && applicability == Account`) because the Muse vendor deliberately omits a weekly duration. The sibling `is_all_model_scope` has the same shape: its `Product` arm is hard-coded to Claude. Each new subscription-usage provider that reports a duration-less weekly window therefore requires a Rust edit in a file unrelated to that provider, and a provider that is added without one silently misses the `weekly_all: always` display policy and stays invisible until its window is nearly spent.

Concrete sites (in the `sase-core` repo, open it with `/sase_repo`):
- `crates/sase_core/src/provider_usage/indicator.rs` — `is_weekly_window` (the `provider == "muse"` arm is around line 827) and `is_all_model_scope`.

Shape of the fix is a design call for the worker: candidates are a declared per-provider classification table shipped alongside the normalizers, a classification hint carried on the observation wire that each normalizer sets, or a provider-capability field. Whatever is chosen must keep the existing Claude/Grok/Muse classifications byte-identical (the `sase-14c` phase-1 tests and the projection-level indicator tests pin them) and must not fabricate a `duration_seconds` for a vendor that omits one.

task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
## Why this is out of scope

Epic sase-14c (Muse Code subscription usage windows) named this in its plan's Risks section: "This change adds a third `provider == "…"` string allowlist arm. That accumulation is worth a follow-up task; it is not a prerequisite for this work and must not expand this epic's scope." The plan's "Out of scope" section repeats it as "Refactoring the accumulated per-provider allowlists in `indicator.rs`". The epic needed exactly one correct arm for Muse; generalizing the mechanism is a separate change with its own design decision and its own blast radius across every usage provider.

payload.description: Epic sase-14c added the third provider == "muse" allowlist arm in indicator.rs and named this refactor in its plan's Risks and Out-of-scope sections

evidence.note: sase-15p (agy usage windows, proposed by phase sase-15p.1) added the FOURTH provider allowlist arm in sase-core indicator.rs: is_weekly_all_window now has provider=="agy" && key=="gemini-weekly" && ModelFamily{family:"gemini"} (sase-core 45a966c). Declared headline-window classification would absorb it.
